assumptions: The flag toggle is treated as causal on the strength of exact-minute correlation plus recovery after the revert; no code-level analysis of the flag's slow path was performed (the code review found nothing to change).
Recovery at 14:39 is attributed to the flag revert. The revert and the observed recovery are only about 30 seconds apart, so a coincidental self-recovery cannot be fully excluded.
Impact is assumed to be limited to account-page requests, since that is the only surface named in the logs and the only one with latency metrics reviewed.

Because only p99 moved, we assume only a small tail of requests was slow and no shopper-visible failures resulted. The ClientDisconnected errors in the logs run at the same rate before and during the window and are treated as pre-existing background noise, not incident impact.

The alternative explanation - that the flag's path calls a slow backing dependency rather than being slow in io-shop itself - was never tested. No such dependency is named in the evidence, so the distinction between 'slow code' and 'slow dependency behind the flag' remains open.
Only 91 minutes of metrics and 35 minutes of logs around the event were examined, so we assume no earlier or related occurrences of the same flag being enabled.
input.executive_summary: For roughly six minutes early on the afternoon of 21 September (14:33-14:39 UTC), the slowest account-page requests on the shop took far longer than normal - worst-case page loads went from about a fifth of a second to between three quarters of a second and a second and a half. Typical page loads, traffic levels and the share of requests that failed were unchanged, so the effect was confined to a small tail of unlucky shoppers viewing their account page; nothing was lost or incorrect, just slow, and no other part of the shop was affected. The cause was a newly switched-on account-page feature. Automated response picked up the alert, traced the slowdown to the minute the feature was enabled, switched it back off, and verified that response times had returned to normal before closing out. A follow-up code review found nothing to fix in the service itself; the feature remains off pending investigation of why its new path is slow.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was toggled from off to on at 14:33 UTC, enabling a slower code path on the io-shop account page; from that exact minute p99 latency stepped from ~200 ms to 755-1530 ms while p50, p95, request volume, memory and error rate all stayed at baseline. Turning the flag back off returned latency to baseline, which confirms the toggle as the trigger.
